Arcelormittal Nippon Steel India Ltd Announces Major Expansion to Boost Domestic Steel Capacity

Arcelormittal Nippon Steel India Ltd has unveiled plans to significantly expand its production capacity with a new investment aimed at meeting growing domestic demand for steel. The company, a leading player in the Indian steel sector, will invest approximately ₹8,000 crore to enhance its existing facilities in Gujarat and Odisha, according to a statement released on Thursday.

The expansion is expected to increase the company’s annual crude steel capacity by 5 million tonnes over the next three years, bringing total output to nearly 20 million tonnes per annum. The initiative comes as India’s construction, automotive, and infrastructure sectors continue to register robust growth, fueling appetite for high-quality steel products.

"India is at the cusp of a major infrastructure transformation. Our decision to invest reflects our confidence in the country’s long-term growth trajectory and our commitment to supporting the ‘Make in India’ vision," said Rajesh Prasad, Chief Operating Officer at Arcelormittal Nippon Steel India Ltd. "With this expansion, we aim not only to serve our existing customers more efficiently but also to tap into emerging markets across the nation."

The announcement was welcomed by industry analysts, who noted that increased capacity could help stabilize domestic steel prices and reduce dependence on imports. "This move positions Arcelormittal Nippon Steel India Ltd as a key driver of capacity growth at a time when India is set to become the world’s second-largest steel producer," said Meera Sethi, a metals sector analyst at Global Markets Research.

The company’s expansion plans include the installation of new energy-efficient blast furnaces, the modernization of rolling mills, and the adoption of advanced environmental management systems. Local suppliers and contractors are expected to benefit from the project, with the company estimating that more than 7,000 direct and indirect jobs will be created during the construction phase.

Trade associations have lauded the decision, emphasizing its potential to spur regional economic development. "We anticipate a positive impact on local economies, particularly in Gujarat and Odisha, where the multiplier effect from such investments is substantial," said Devashish Rao, President of the Federation of Steel Producers.

Arcelormittal Nippon Steel India Ltd’s expansion aligns with the government’s National Steel Policy, which targets a capacity of 300 million tonnes by 2030. Completion of the new facilities is scheduled for late 2027, with phased commissioning set to begin in 2025.
